description:
Factory AI GMO's commercial platform needs a way for a signed-up person to create and manage an Organization — the workspace under which they will later create Projects and run the Software Construction Factory. This is the foundational entity for the entire authenticated side of the commercial platform: every other authenticated capability described in the commercialization plan (projects, factory runs, generated artifacts, validation results, usage, billing) belongs to an Organization, not to a person directly. This is the first module of Factory AI GMO's own Commercial App, built by the Software Construction Factory itself, following the same two-factory architecture already established for leadCapture: the Software Factory constructs software; a separate Commercial Factory (not yet built) will later turn that software into customers and revenue.

BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS
- An authenticated person can create a new Organization, becoming its owner.
- An Organization has a human-readable name and a unique, URL-safe handle used to reference it in the platform's own URLs and API calls.
- An Organization has a subscription/plan tier and a lifecycle status, since the commercialization plan explicitly calls for future usage-based billing and the ability to suspend or cancel an account.
- Authorized members of an Organization can view and update its own details (name, plan awareness, status) — this module does not yet cover inviting additional members, which is a related but separate capability.

CONSTRAINTS — already decided, satisfy them rather than re-deciding them
- This is a genuinely different product line from the POS GMO retail platform. An Organization here is a *commercial-platform tenant* (a Factory AI GMO customer's workspace), not a POS GMO retail business — it must not be confused with, or implemented as, the existing `companies` table, which represents POS GMO's own existing retail tenants.
- created_At/updated_at remain server-controlled, same convention as every other module in this repository.

OPEN ARCHITECTURAL QUESTIONS — deliberately unresolved; do not silently pick an answer and hide the ambiguity
1. Ownership/identity: this commercial platform has no existing users/accounts table of its own — the platform's actual signed-up people don't exist as data yet anywhere in this system. How an Organization's owner is modeled (a real foreign key once an accounts/identity module exists, vs. some interim reference) is an open question this PRD deliberately does not resolve. Do not invent a `users` table as a side effect of this PRD, and do not silently assume POS GMO's existing `companies`/employee/user tables can stand in for it — they belong to a different product and a different tenancy model entirely (see Experiment 1-7's `companyId` findings for exactly why silently reusing an existing tenancy assumption for a new, different one caused real, traced defects).
2. Role model: this platform's authenticated side needs its own role vocabulary (something like Organization Owner / Admin / Member), which does not exist anywhere in this factory's current schema — the only roles this repository's PRD format can express (Admin, Manager, Cashier) are POS GMO retail-operations roles and do not fit this product. `roles_allowed` below is set to the closest available value only because the schema requires *a* value from that fixed list; it is not a real design decision about this platform's actual access model, and should not be treated as one downstream.
3. Slug unique­ness and generation: whether the slug is user-supplied, system-generated from the name, or both (with collision handling) is not specified here — an open design question for the Architect/Database agents to decide and justify, the same way duplicate-lead handling was left open for leadCapture.
4. Plan/billing enforcement: this module only records which plan tier an Organization is on. Whether or how that tier is actually enforced (feature gating, usage limits, payment integration) is explicitly out of scope for this PRD and must not be invented here.

This PRD intentionally leaves architecture decisions (schema shape, relationships, endpoints beyond standard CRUD) to the Architect/Database/Backend agents, consistent with the commercialization plan's own instruction that 'the exact modules and schema should be discovered and designed by the Software Factory from the commercial requirements rather than assumed in advance.'

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable Organization name, e.g. 'Acme Retail Group'.

fields.name: slug
fields.description: URL-safe unique handle for this Organization, used in the commercial platform's own URLs and API references. Whether it's user-supplied, system-generated, or both is an open design question — see description.

fields.name: ownerEmail
fields.description: Email of the person who created and owns this Organization. This platform has no existing users/accounts table — how ownership is ultimately modeled (a real relationship once an accounts system exists, vs. this interim reference) is an open architectural question, not something this field should be read as having settled.

fields.name: plan
fields.description: Subscription/plan tier, e.g. free, pro, enterprise. Allowed values and their meaning are not prescribed here. Billing enforcement itself is out of scope for this PRD.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Organization lifecycle state, e.g. active, suspended, canceled. Defaults to active on creation. Transition rules (who can suspend/cancel, and whether a canceled Organization can be reactivated) are an open design question, not specified here.
